verdict.rationale: Cua documents two ways for an agent to work behind a login. A signed-in app such as Chrome or Slack can move into a Space and stay signed in, so the agent inherits the session instead of receiving credentials. A locked saved-password store can also let an agent sign in to a site, with approval and Touch ID gating for sensitive items. However, no evidence states that the credential values are kept out of the model's context or out of logs. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that credentials never reach the model or its logs, details of how the vault injects credentials, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an operator, the agent can work behind logins without my credentials passing through the model or its logs

citations.quote: Move a signed-in app, such as Chrome or Slack, into a Space and it opens there still signed in.
Every item is locked until you allow unattended access. Approve requests, lock or delete items, let an agent sign in to a site with a saved password
Nothing is read until you approve, and sensitive items need Touch ID.
